description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between "Initial Confidence" and "Accuracy" across three different metrics: Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," utilizes a linear scale ranging from 0.91 to 0.99, with tick marks placed at regular intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," also employs a linear scale with visible tick labels ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 at intervals of 0.2, while the gridlines extend up to 1.0. The plot features three distinct lines, all of which include vertical error bars at each data point. The "Final Accuracy" is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; it begins at approximately 0.91 on the y-axis at an x-value of 0.91, reaches a peak of roughly 0.99 at x=0.93, dips to about 0.86 at x=0.96, and concludes at approximately 0.92 at x=0.99. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" is depicted by a dashed orange line with diamond markers, starting at roughly 0.55 at x=0.91, peaking at about 0.67 at x=0.92, and then generally declining to its lowest point of approximately 0.10 at x=0.98 before ending at roughly 0.16 at x=0.99. Finally, the "Initial Accuracy" is shown as a dash-dot green line with square markers; it starts at approximately 0.36 at x=0.91, dips to its lowest point of about 0.27 at x=0.92, and then exhibits a general upward trend, peaking at roughly 0.87 at x=0.98 before finishing at approximately 0.77 at x=0.99.
